answer_text:
Let

\[
I_n=\int_{[0,1]^n}\max(x_1,x_2,\dots,x_n)\,dx_1dx_2\cdots dx_n.
\]

The integral is the expectation of the maximum of \(n\) independent uniform random variables on \([0,1]\).

For \(t\in[0,1]\),

\[
\max(x_1,\dots,x_n)\le t
\iff
0\le x_1,x_2,\dots,x_n\le t.
\]

Thus the volume of the set where the maximum is at most \(t\) is

\[
t^n.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\mathbb{P}(\max(x_1,\dots,x_n)>t)=1-t^n.
\]

For a nonnegative bounded random variable \(M\),

\[
\mathbb{E}[M]=\int_0^1 \mathbb{P}(M>t)\,dt.
\]

Applying this with \(M=\max(x_1,\dots,x_n)\),

\[
I_n=\int_0^1 (1-t^n)\,dt.
\]

Now compute:

\[
I_n=\left[t-\frac{t^{n+1}}{n+1}\right]_0^1
=1-\frac{1}{n+1}
=\frac{n}{n+1}.
\]

Hence,

\[
\boxed{\frac{n}{n+1}}
\]
